scenario.name: Scan a sideloaded shelf and make one book readable
scenario.audience: one reader who sideloads DRM-free EPUB and MOBI files from mixed sources
scenario.objective: Turn a folder of stray e-book files into a persistent, searchable shelf and open one book in a reading app.
workflow: Point the library at a local folder of e-book files and start a scan
Review the created entries and correct a title or author that was derived badly
Put the entry in a collection and locate it again with a field-qualified search
Use the entry's file through the download/handoff path to read it
acceptance: One scan produces one book entry per work with its cover, and a second scan adds no duplicate entries
The corrected metadata and collection assignment survive a restart of the library
A search on the corrected author or title returns that entry
The entry's file opens through the read/download path

license_uncertainties: Design reference only; no source code copied; file-level exceptions not exhaustively audited.
excluded_paths: Unselected files; upstream not installed or run

feedback.error: independent review did not pass; retain candidate and findings

observations.reason: library.py:60-72 confirms filter_books calls scan_folder, populates file_list with walked paths, then filters with the unescaped regex \.epub|\.mobi|\.pdf; no content hash or work-level key is computed in that path.

library.py:309-328 confirms compare_shelf_current obtains stored Book.file_name values via Storage.book_paths_list and returns the set difference between on-disk and stored paths, so the upstream suppression is path-based rather than content-based.
library.py:114-123 confirms the no-dc:title fallback takes the final path component and removes the extension, then applies the Book-prefix regex split before use.

storage.py:277-295 confirms fields title, author, and tags, field:value and field:quoted-value parsing, and a keywords bucket for non-field bare/quoted tokens; unknown field prefixes are silently discarded upstream, which the target design deliberately replaces with 422 unknown_field.
storage.py:297-332 confirms case-insensitive substring matching for requested fields via match_field, then rapidfuzz process.extract with fuzz.WRatio and a score > 50 filter for keyword queries.
storage.py:68-111 confirms insert_book uses one SQLAlchemy Session per book, reads cover bytes from book[2].data or book[2], commits, and logs and returns False when an exception occurs.
models.py:19-42 confirms the Book model stores one file_name string plus title, optional author, cover bytes, tags, categories, and a book_collections relationship to BookCollection.

README.md:21-36 confirms the documented feature list: recursive scanning, cover aggregation, fuzzy search with tag/author/title specifiers, download, folder-derived collections, and epub/mobi support.

issues: Entry removal is omitted even though the leaf lists it as defining core: leaf.md:163-169 explicitly includes 'removal of entries' under 'Defining core — without these, not an e-book library', while the architecture §15 (VIEW_ARCH.md:166-168) and the authored gap (REVIEW_SCOPE.md:136-139, AUTHOR_INPUT.json:94) deliberately exclude removal. The fixed scan/correct/collection/search/download scenario does not exercise removal, but the template is presented as a core-usable e-book library and its own gap acknowledges the conflict. Explicit disclosure does not satisfy the leaf core. Add a minimal removal contract and acceptance (at least catalog-only removal, or entry-plus-file removal with a documented file policy), or explicitly narrow the template to a scenario slice and stop claiming the full leaf core.
review.summary: The scenario specification and probe are strong: A01-A04 cover scan, covers, duplicate suppression, failure isolation, revision conflict, correction, collection assignment, restart durability, field-qualified search with negative and unsupported-field cases, and exact-byte file handoff. All eight upstream observations match the fixed source bytes, and the Node/Fastify/SQLite design is clearly separated from the GPL pyShelf evidence with no execution or certification claims. One blocking scope defect remains: the template omits entry removal, which leaf.md lists as defining core, and only records that omission as a gap. The template is not core-usable as claimed until a minimal removal path and acceptance are added, or its scope is explicitly narrowed.

revision.scope: Fix existing core violations only; preserve fixed scenario, sources and delivery profile.
